val titles = listOf("Mr", "Mme", "Melle")
val hobbies = listOf("sport", "music", "reading", "cinema")
val countries = mapOf("fr" to "France", "be" to "Belgium", "ch" to "Switzerland")
val languages = mapOf("fr" to "French", "en" to "English", "es" to "Spanish")

// all the values, gathered in one object (what would be sent to a server).
// @Serializable: the kotlinx.serialization plugin can convert it to JSON
@Serializable
data class Model(
    val title: String,
    val name: String,
    val age: Int?,
    val presentation: String,
    val newsletter: Boolean,
    val hobbies: List<String>,
    val country: String,
    val languages: List<String>,
    val birthDate: String?,
    val satisfaction: Int,
)

// the JSON converter: prettyPrint, indented JSON
val indentedJson = Json { prettyPrint = true }

class Ex05Activity : ComponentActivity() {
    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        enableEdgeToEdge()
        setContent { ExamplesTheme { FormPage() } }
    }
}

@Composable
fun FormPage() {
    // one state per field of the form
    var title by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("Mme") }
    var name by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") }
    var age by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("30") }
    var presentation by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") } // the VALIDATED value
    var draft by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("") } // the text being typed
    var newsletter by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }
    var myHobbies by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf("reading")) } // a SET: no duplicate
    var myCountry by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("fr") }
    var myLanguages by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(setOf<String>()) }
    var birthDate by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<LocalDate?>(null) } // null: not chosen yet
    var satisfaction by rememberSaveable { mutableFloatStateOf(3f) }
    var sent by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    var calendarOpen by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }

    // the model: a value COMPUTED from the state
    val model = Model(
        title = title,
        name = name.trim(),
        age = age.toIntOrNull(), // null if the field is empty
        presentation = presentation,
        newsletter = newsletter,
        hobbies = myHobbies.toList(),
        country = myCountry,
        languages = myLanguages.toList(),
        birthDate = birthDate?.toString(), // "2026-10-05": the date format of the RdvMedecins API
        satisfaction = satisfaction.toInt(),
    )
    val titleStyle = MaterialTheme.typography.titleSmall

    ExamplePage("Example 05 - controlled fields") {
        Text("Title", style = titleStyle)
        // selectableGroup: a group of radio buttons (for accessibility)
        Row(Modifier.selectableGroup(), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
            for (t in titles) {
                // selectable: the WHOLE line (button + text) reacts to the press
                Row(
                    verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically,
                    modifier = Modifier.selectable(selected = title == t, onClick = { title = t }, role = Role.RadioButton),
                ) {
                    RadioButton(selected = title == t, onClick = null)
                    Text(t)
                    Spacer(Modifier.width(12.dp))
                }
            }
        }
        Row {
            OutlinedTextField(value = name, onValueChange = { name = it }, label = { Text("Name") }, modifier = Modifier.weight(2f))
            Spacer(Modifier.width(12.dp))
            OutlinedTextField(
                value = age,
                onValueChange = { age = it },
                label = { Text("Age") },
                keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number),
                modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
            )
        }
        // onFocusChanged: notifies when the field GAINS or LOSES the focus. The
        // presentation is only copied into the state when leaving the field
        OutlinedTextField(
            value = draft,
            onValueChange = { draft = it },
            label = { Text("Presentation (updated when leaving the field)") },
            minLines = 2,
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().onFocusChanged { state ->
                if (!state.isFocused) presentation = draft
            },
        )
        // a single box: true / false. toggleable: the whole line reacts
        ListItem(
            modifier = Modifier.toggleable(value = newsletter, onValueChange = { newsletter = it }, role = Role.Checkbox),
            leadingContent = { Checkbox(checked = newsletter, onCheckedChange = null) },
            headlineContent = { Text("Receive the newsletter") },
        )
        Text("Hobbies", style = titleStyle)
        // several chips for ONE set: the value is added or removed
        FlowRow(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            for (h in hobbies) {
                FilterChip(
                    selected = h in myHobbies,
                    onClick = { myHobbies = if (h in myHobbies) myHobbies - h else myHobbies + h },
                    label = { Text(h) },
                )
            }
        }
        // a drop-down list: value says which element is chosen
        DropdownList(
            label = "Country",
            value = myCountry,
            choices = countries.keys.toList(),
            text = { code -> countries.getValue(code) },
            onChange = { myCountry = it },
            modifier = Modifier.width(220.dp),
        )
        Text("Spoken languages", style = titleStyle)
        FlowRow(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            for ((code, label) in languages) {
                FilterChip(
                    selected = code in myLanguages,
                    onClick = { myLanguages = if (code in myLanguages) myLanguages - code else myLanguages + code },
                    label = { Text(label) },
                )
            }
        }
        Row(verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
            Text("Satisfaction: ${satisfaction.toInt()} / 5", style = titleStyle)
            // a slider from 1 to 5: 3 intermediate steps (2, 3, 4)
            Slider(
                value = satisfaction,
                onValueChange = { satisfaction = it },
                valueRange = 1f..5f,
                steps = 3,
                modifier = Modifier.weight(1f).padding(start = 8.dp),
            )
        }
        ListItem(
            leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.DateRange, contentDescription = null) },
            headlineContent = { Text("Date of birth") },
            supportingContent = { Text(birthDate?.toString() ?: "not chosen") },
            trailingContent = { OutlinedButton(onClick = { calendarOpen = true }) { Text("Choose") } },
        )
        // FlowRow: the buttons wrap to the next line on a narrow screen
        FlowRow(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
            Button(onClick = { sent = Json.encodeToString(Model.serializer(), model) }) { Text("Send") }
            // the state modified BY THE CODE: the fields follow
            OutlinedButton(onClick = {
                title = "Mr"
                name = "MARTIN"
                age = "42"
                myHobbies = setOf("sport", "cinema")
                myCountry = "be"
            }) { Text("Fill in by code") }
        }
        Spacer(Modifier.height(8.dp))
        Text("The model, live", style = titleStyle)
        Text(
            indentedJson.encodeToString(Model.serializer(), model),
            fontFamily = FontFamily.Monospace,
            fontSize = 12.sp,
            modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().background(Color(0xFFF5F5F5)).padding(8.dp),
        )
        // a block that only exists after a submission; ?.let: only if sent is not null
        sent?.let { json ->
            Text("Last submission", style = titleStyle)
            Text(
                json,
                fontFamily = FontFamily.Monospace,
                fontSize = 12.sp,
                modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth().background(Color(0xFFE8F5E9)).padding(8.dp),
            )
        }
    }

    // the calendar dialog: it only exists if calendarOpen is true
    if (calendarOpen) {
        // the state of the calendar: the selected date, in milliseconds (UTC)
        val calendarState = rememberDatePickerState(
            initialSelectedDateMillis = (birthDate ?: LocalDate.of(2000, 1, 1)).atStartOfDay(ZoneOffset.UTC).toInstant().toEpochMilli(),
        )
        DatePickerDialog(
            onDismissRequest = { calendarOpen = false },
            confirmButton = {
                TextButton(onClick = {
                    calendarState.selectedDateMillis?.let { ms ->
                        birthDate = Instant.ofEpochMilli(ms).atZone(ZoneOffset.UTC).toLocalDate()
                    }
                    calendarOpen = false
                }) { Text("OK") }
            },
            dismissButton = { TextButton(onClick = { calendarOpen = false }) { Text("Cancel") } },
        ) {
            DatePicker(state = calendarState)
        }
    }
}
  • lines 89–101: all form values, grouped into a class [@Serializable]: the [kotlinx.serialization] plugin generates code at compile time that converts it to JSON ([Json.encodeToString(Model.serializer(), model)]);
  • Lines 118–130: one state per field. [myHobbies] is an unmodifiable SET ([Set]): [myHobbies + h] and [myHobbies - h] generate new ones; [birthDate] is a “nullable” date ([LocalDate?]): [null] until a value is selected;
  • lines 133–143: the model, a value COMPUTED on each execution; [toIntOrNull()]: the number, or [null] if the text is not a number;
  • lines 150–157: radio buttons. [Modifier.selectable] makes the WHOLE line (the button and the text) clickable; the button itself therefore has no action ([onClick = null]); [selectableGroup] groups the buttons for accessibility tools;
  • Lines 177–182: The presentation is copied into the state only when LEAVING the field; [onFocusChanged] triggers a notification when the field gains or loses focus;
  • lines 187–189: a checkbox, which works the same way as radio buttons ([Modifier.toggleable] across the entire line);
  • lines 193–198: checkboxes ([FilterChip]) for selecting multiple values; [FlowRow] wraps them to the next line if there isn’t enough space;
  • lines 203–208: the drop-down list from [common/];
  • lines 224–228: a slider from 1 to 5: [steps = 3] with intermediate steps;
  • lines 236–248: “Fill in by code”: the state is modified, and the fields follow;
  • lines 251–259: the model displayed in JSON, indented ([Json [ prettyPrint = true ]]); [sent?.let [ ... ]]: the block exists only if [sent] is not [null];
  • Lines 271–288: The calendar window exists only if [calendarOpen] is true. [DatePicker] operates in milliseconds since January 1, 1970 (time UTC): conversion works both ways with [java.time] ([LocalDate], [Instant], [ZoneOffset.UTC]).

The calendar ([DatePickerDialog]) is in English: [Material 3] follows the application’s language (see Example 21).

docs.title: 3.6. Example 06: A form, an object, a reducer
docs.text:
Example 05 had one state variable per field. For a real form, we prefer ONE object that contains all the values, and we describe its changes in a single PURE function, the REDUCER: [reducer(currentState, action) -> newState]. The screen no longer modifies the state: it reports what has happened (“the LASTNAME field now has the value ‘Dupont’,” “the LASTNAME field has been exited”), and the reducer deduces the new state from this.

// =========================================================================
// ex06/Ex06Activity.kt - a form, an object, a reducer
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Example 05 had one state variable per field of the form. For a
// real form, we prefer ONE object that contains all the values, the
// MODEL (here a Profile object, unmodifiable), and we describe its
// changes in a single function, the REDUCER:
//
//     reducer(currentState, action) -> newState
//
// The screen no longer modifies the state: it DESCRIBES what happened, with a
// ProfileAction object (Update(Field.LASTNAME, "Dupont"), Leave(Field.LASTNAME)...),
// and the reducer deduces the new state from it. All the logic is in one
// place, in a PURE function (same input, same output, no side
// effect), easy to test.
// Kotlin is well suited to it: a "sealed" interface lists all the possible
// actions, and a when on an action is checked by the compiler (a
// forgotten case is an error).
//
// The state also keeps, for each field, whether it has been "touched" (left at
// least once); from that we deduce whether it is "modified" (its value differs from
// the initial value) and whether it is disabled.
// =========================================================================
@file:OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class, ExperimentalLayoutApi::class)

import android.os.Bundle
